macos.rationale: IDE supports macOS Intel/Apple Silicon, Windows 10/11 x64/ARM64 and listed modern Linux distributions; Crew has separate desktop support. Scope: Kiro CLI, Kiro Crew, Kiro IDE, Kiro mobile preview, Kiro Web.

windows.rationale: IDE supports macOS Intel/Apple Silicon, Windows 10/11 x64/ARM64 and listed modern Linux distributions; Crew has separate desktop support. Scope: Kiro CLI, Kiro Crew, Kiro IDE, Kiro mobile preview, Kiro Web.

linux.rationale: IDE supports macOS Intel/Apple Silicon, Windows 10/11 x64/ARM64 and listed modern Linux distributions; Crew has separate desktop support. Scope: Kiro CLI, Kiro Crew, Kiro IDE, Kiro mobile preview, Kiro Web.

web-client.rationale: Kiro Web uses a modern browser without local installation. Scope: Kiro CLI, Kiro Crew, Kiro IDE, Kiro mobile preview, Kiro Web.

cli.rationale: CLI supports macOS, Windows 11 PowerShell and Linux glibc 2.34+ or musl variants. Scope: Kiro CLI, Kiro Crew, Kiro IDE, Kiro mobile preview, Kiro Web.

local.rationale: Crew runs on the user's machine, container or controlled remote host; the desktop app can connect through an SSH tunnel. Scope: Kiro CLI, Kiro Crew, Kiro IDE, Kiro mobile preview, Kiro Web.

own-server.rationale: Crew runs on the user's machine, container or controlled remote host; the desktop app can connect through an SSH tunnel. Scope: Kiro CLI, Kiro Crew, Kiro IDE, Kiro mobile preview, Kiro Web.

vendor-cloud.rationale: Sessions run in isolated Kiro cloud sandboxes in us-east-1; a paid Pro-family plan and some organization enablement are required. Scope: Kiro CLI, Kiro Crew, Kiro IDE, Kiro mobile preview, Kiro Web.

parallel-runs.rationale: Spec task execution can run independent tasks in parallel on IDE, CLI and Web; the matrix excludes mobile. Scope: Kiro CLI, Kiro IDE, Kiro mobile preview, Kiro Web.

coordinator.rationale: Crew can spawn isolated subagents and synthesize their results; this does not establish IDE-native delegation parity. Scope: Kiro Crew.

unattended-triggers.rationale: Crew Schedule creates recurring jobs in separate sessions; continued execution depends on its Gateway host. Scope: Kiro Crew, Kiro Web.

pr-workflow.rationale: The Web spec flow implements tasks and opens a PR or merge request, with later feedback updates. Scope: Kiro CLI, Kiro IDE, Kiro Web.

free-tier.rationale: Kiro Free provides fifty credits monthly for limited listed models; cloud/Web access is not implied. Scope: Kiro CLI, Kiro Crew, Kiro IDE, Kiro mobile preview, Kiro Web.

starting-price.rationale: Kiro Free provides fifty credits monthly for limited listed models; cloud/Web access is not implied. Scope: Kiro CLI, Kiro Crew, Kiro IDE, Kiro mobile preview, Kiro Web.

laptop-independent.rationale: Disconnecting a client does not stop an in-flight cloud task according to the guide. Scope: Kiro CLI, Kiro Crew, Kiro IDE, Kiro mobile preview, Kiro Web.

claude-code.rationale: Crew Developer Mode Preview explicitly runs this coding harness; backend limitations remain in receipt.

codex.rationale: Crew Developer Mode Preview runs Codex through its ACP adapter, with sandbox required.

opencode.rationale: Crew Developer Mode Preview executes the opencode binary.

pi.rationale: Crew Developer Mode Preview requires pi and pi-acp; Crew MCP tools are unavailable.

cursor.rationale: The complete documented native harness list and released registry are closed to the listed Kiro/Crew backends. The registry rejects arbitrary IDs and omits cursor. Configured MCP tools and model-provider choice do not add a coding harness.

gemini-cli.rationale: The complete documented native harness list and released registry are closed to the listed Kiro/Crew backends. The registry rejects arbitrary IDs and omits gemini-cli. Configured MCP tools and model-provider choice do not add a coding harness.

grok.rationale: The complete documented native harness list and released registry are closed to the listed Kiro/Crew backends. The registry rejects arbitrary IDs and omits grok. Configured MCP tools and model-provider choice do not add a coding harness.

aider.rationale: The complete documented native harness list and released registry are closed to the listed Kiro/Crew backends. The registry rejects arbitrary IDs and omits aider. Configured MCP tools and model-provider choice do not add a coding harness.

antigravity.rationale: The complete documented native harness list and released registry are closed to the listed Kiro/Crew backends. The registry rejects arbitrary IDs and omits antigravity. Configured MCP tools and model-provider choice do not add a coding harness.

worktree.rationale: Crew Task Runner creates per-run Git worktrees in existing repositories.

container.rationale: Crew documents running the Gateway/agent system in Docker.

vm.rationale: The first-party architecture names a VM for managed cloud execution. No containment strength is inferred.

issue-tracking.rationale: Crew Task Runner has durable task IDs and states spanning per-step sessions, with persistent queue/checkpoints.

license.rationale: Main Kiro IDE/CLI use AWS Content/IP terms; dependency or separate Crew licensing does not replace them.

self-hosting.rationale: Crew core Gateway and state run on customer hardware, service or Docker; selected backend dependencies remain.

telemetry-opt-out.rationale: Explicit IDE and CLI telemetry-off controls are separate from content collection.

sso.rationale: Kiro organization sign-in supports IAM Identity Center and external identity providers.

review-ui.rationale: IDE supervised mode exposes proposed changes for review and approval.

subscription.rationale: Pro $20, Pro+ $40, Pro Max $100, Power $200 monthly.

no-paid-plan.rationale: The complete Kiro pricing lineup has recurring individual and team paid tiers plus credit add-ons, with no no-paid-plan plan.

one-time.rationale: The complete Kiro pricing lineup has recurring individual and team paid tiers plus credit add-ons, with no one-time plan.

compute.rationale: Managed cloud compute is explicitly included in paid credits with no separate cloud compute charge.

byok.rationale: Crew Strands explicitly accepts the user model-provider keys in Settings Secrets. This applies to an external Crew backend, not managed Kiro inference.

ios.rationale: Requested and limited TestFlight invitations are not a publicly available native iPhone release under the platform availability rule.

android.rationale: The current availability table links a public Android 10+ Google Play release; a paid Kiro tier is required.

mobile-web.rationale: Crew explicitly documents opening its user-hosted HTTPS dashboard in a phone browser.

byo-subscription.rationale: Crew delegates to native Claude Code and Codex sign-in with their own account credential stores; this is external agent-account reuse rather than Kiro credits or API keys alone.

multiplayer.rationale: The shipped opt-in Shared Crew preview admits distinct verified people who can prompt the same session. Scope is Crew, not same-account managed cross-device continuity.

roles.rationale: Organization administrators manage users, groups and pooled credit limits; this establishes an admin/member distinction.
